An artist is a person who creates works of art — things made to express ideas, feelings, beauty, or meaning, rather than simply to serve a practical purpose.

The key word here is express. An artist isn't just making something that functions. They are communicating something — an emotion, a thought, a vision, a story, or a truth about the world — through their chosen medium.
What Counts as "Art"?

Art is any creative work made with skill and imagination to produce an experience — visual, emotional, intellectual, or sensory — in the audience. This includes:

  • Visual works — paintings, drawings, sculptures, photographs, prints
  • Performed works — music, dance, theatre, opera
  • Written works — poetry, literary fiction, screenplays
  • Newer forms — film, digital art, installation art, video art

So an artist is the person behind any of these. A painter, a sculptor, a musician, a dancer, a poet, a filmmaker — all are artists.
The Two Things That Define an Artist

An artist is identified by two essential qualities:

  1. Skill — they have developed an ability in their craft, whether through formal training or self-teaching.
  2. Creative expression — they bring their own imagination, voice, and perspective to their work. They aren't simply copying or mechanically repeating. Something personal and original is present in what they make.

Without skill, a person may have good ideas but cannot execute them well. Without creative expression, a person may be technically excellent but is more of a technician than an artist. A true artist has both.
Artist vs. Artisan — An Important Distinction

These two words are often confused.

An artisan (or craftsperson) is someone who makes things with great technical skill — a furniture maker, a tailor, a jeweller, a glassblower. They follow established techniques and produce objects that are beautiful and useful.

An artist, on the other hand, prioritizes personal expression and originality. Their work is not primarily functional — it is meant to be experienced, felt, or contemplated.

That said, the line between the two can blur. A master potter who puts deep creative vision into every piece they make can rightfully be called an artist. And a painter who mass-produces identical copies of a painting is behaving more like a craftsperson. The distinction is about intent and originality, not the medium.
Does an Artist Have to Work Professionally?

No. Being an artist is not about earning a living from art. Someone who paints purely as a hobby, with skill and personal expression, is still an artist. The label describes what a person does and how they do it, not whether they get paid for it.

However, in some contexts — especially in the music industry — you will hear the term recording artist, which does specifically refer to a professional who records and releases music commercially.
Narrow vs. Broad Uses

The word "artist" is sometimes used narrowly to refer only to visual artists — painters and sculptors especially. In everyday conversation, if someone says "my friend is an artist," many people will picture someone who paints or draws.

But in formal and educated usage, the word is broad — it applies to any creative person across all art forms: musicians, writers, actors, dancers, filmmakers, and more.

Context usually makes it clear which meaning is intended.
The Figurative Use

"Artist" is also used figuratively — outside the world of art — to describe someone who does any activity with exceptional creativity and skill, almost as if it were an art form.

"He's an absolute artist with a scalpel." (a very skilled surgeon)
"Watch her cook — she's a true artist." (someone who cooks with extraordinary flair)

This use is a compliment. It says the person doesn't just do their job competently — they elevate it to something beautiful or extraordinary.
One Negative Use: "Con Artist"

You will also encounter the phrase con artist — and this is important to know, because it has nothing to do with creativity or beauty.

A con artist is a person who deceives and tricks others for personal gain, usually money. The word "con" is short for "confidence" — they gain your trust, then exploit it. The word "artist" here is used sarcastically, meaning they are "skilled" at deception. This is a fixed, well-known phrase and does not change the general meaning of "artist."
Other Common Compounds

• Performing artist — someone who performs live (musician, dancer, actor)
  • Makeup artist — a professional who applies makeup, especially for film, theatre, or fashion
  • Tattoo artist — someone who creates tattoos as a skilled, creative practice
  • Martial artist — someone highly skilled in a martial art (like karate or judo) — again a figurative extension
Summary

An artist is a person who creates works — visual, musical, literary, or performative — with skill and original creative expression, with the aim of producing an aesthetic experience or communicating something meaningful. The word can be used narrowly (for painters and sculptors) or broadly (for any creative practitioner). It extends figuratively to anyone who brings extraordinary creativity and mastery to any activity.
